title: After
summary: Spring, some months later. Sunday soup has become a long table. The sealed letter opens. The Critic sits beside Théo, small and quiet. The story hands itself to the player. The only chapter in full colour.

screens.image: FIRST FULL-COLOUR PAGE. The courtyard in spring: wisteria, sun, a long table made of three tables pushed together, mismatched chairs, bunting.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Spring.

screens.image: Wide view: everyone at the long table. Madame Roux at the head, Yann with bread, Sophie and Trois-Pattes, Lucien with a crossword, Nadia, Béa, Hugo, Karim.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Sunday soup has grown a bit.

objects.label: Madame Roux
objects.line: Has started teaching Karim her soup.

objects.label: Yann
objects.line: Now brings two kinds of bread. He's showing off.

objects.label: Lucien
objects.line: Has finished every crossword since Christmas, with help.

objects.label: Nadia
objects.line: Signed the lease on her tattoo studio. The octopus is in the window.

objects.label: Hugo
objects.line: Fifth career. Still has his sheep.

objects.label: Karim
objects.line: Comes every week. Brought a friend.

screens.image: Camille arriving through the archway with a bottle of wine and a big scarf.

words.speaker: Camille
words.text: So THIS is the famous soup.

screens.image: Théo and Camille hugging, everyone watching, smiling.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Théo introduces his sister to everyone. It takes a while. He has a lot of people to introduce now.

screens.image: Théo at the big pot, ladling, glowing; Camille watching him, proud.

words.speaker: Camille
words.text: You look like you again.

words.speaker: Théo
words.text: I think I look like a new me. The old one didn't know how to do this.

screens.image: Madame Roux pulling Théo aside, finger raised as usual.

words.speaker: Madame Roux
words.text: You know, the bakery on the corner is looking for someone in the kitchen. Early mornings. I told them about you. Don't be angry.

options.label: "Why would I be angry? Thank you."

screens.image: Théo looking at the long table, thoughtful.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Théo doesn't know yet what he'll do with his life. The {chased} was a plan. This isn't a plan. It's a direction: toward people, with food.

screens.image: Marie-Clo's office, the window open, spring light.

words.speaker: Marie-Clo
words.text: Shall we try once a month instead of every two weeks?

screens.image: Théo in the chair, relaxed.

words.speaker: Théo
words.text: Yeah. I think so.

words.speaker: Marie-Clo
words.text: Tell me what you've learned about people this month.

words.speaker: Théo
words.text: How long have you got?

screens.image: The curiosity notebook, now fat, pages bristling with tabs.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: The curiosity notebook is full. Not of Théo's pain. Of other people's lives.

screens.image: Théo's desk drawer, the sealed envelope with red wax.

text.ready: And then, one evening, the date arrives.
text.waiting: The letter isn't ready yet. Théo will open it on {letterDate}. So will you.

screens.image: The wax seal cracking.
The letter in the player's own words, in handwriting font, on cream paper.
Théo reading at the window, the sunset over the full-colour city.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: The Théo who wrote this was on a kitchen floor. He couldn't eat. He didn't know if there would be a later. There was. He's reading it.

interaction.prompt: Write back to the Théo of then. What would you tell him? (optional)

screens.image: The park bench under the plane trees. Théo sitting. The Critic sitting beside him, pebble-sized, in a tiny scarf.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: The Critic is still around. It probably always will be.

screens.image: Close: the Critic looking up at Théo, worried eyes.

words.speaker: Critic
words.text: What if it all falls apart again?

screens.image: Théo patting the bench beside the Critic.

words.speaker: Théo
words.text: It might. Then I'll know what to do. And I'll know who to call.

screens.image: The Critic leaning on Théo's leg, eyes closing. The pain creature from Chapter 2, tiny, curled up on the other side.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: The Critic doesn't say anything else. For once, it doesn't need to.

screens.image: The Light Map in full colour: the whole city at dusk, dozens of lit windows, Théo's own window glowing brightest.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Théo's map. Every window, a person. Most of them were strangers once.

screens.image: The narrator turning to face out: a full-page hand-drawn frame around an empty space where the player's phone camera would see them (no camera used; just an empty warm frame).

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: This was Théo's story. But you've been doing the quests too. The questions, the walks, the doors you stood outside.

screens.image: The empty frame, warm light spilling out.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: So here's the last thing. This is your story now. Keep lighting the lamp. The boats are out there, even when you can't see them.

screens.image: A long table in a courtyard, an empty chair at the end with a bowl in front of it.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: There's a place for you at the table.

screens.image: End card: hand-lettered "After", a soup bowl, steam drawn as a little heart.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: The end. Or rather: the beginning of the after.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: {dedication}

screens.image: Ongoing card, drawn as a small lamp.

interaction.title: Keep the lamp lit
interaction.text: One small weekly quest from now on: go back somewhere, ask someone a real question, cook for someone, or check on someone. All chapters stay open to reread.
